key_insight: ToolSciVer improves multimodal scientific claim verification by teaching a VLM to choose the right visual tool for tables, charts, and dense figure regions, turning hard-to-read scientific visuals into explicit evidence for reasoning.
engineering_relevance: The paper offers a practical blueprint for building more reliable document AI systems in scientific workflows, where accurate evidence extraction from complex figures and tables is often the bottleneck.
method: Adds three type-aware visual tools: table row/column focus, chart-to-structure parsing, and high-resolution region zoom.
Trains tool selection with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) using a composite reward for correctness, format validity, length control, tool efficiency, and tool-validity penalties.
Integrates tool outputs into claim-facing evidence for multimodal reasoning in a VLM.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on SciVer and MuSciClaims across five VLMs from Qwen, InternVL, and Gemma families, outperforming four competitive baselines in the abstract.
watch_item: The approach adds policy and tool-chain complexity, so gains may depend on robust tool invocation, clean formatting, and reliable parsing of scientific visuals at inference time.
paper_title: ToolSciVer: Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification with Visual Tool Augmented Reinforcement Learning
